subject: Dedicated capacity planning: Lumenify supply-match matrix, tokens/sec & SLO headroom
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@lumenify.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity planning: initial supply-match matrix and asks

Sara — thanks again for the time earlier. As promised I'm sending a first-pass supply-match worksheet and a short list of inputs we need from you to finalize GPU sizing for the Dedicated commitment. The attached workbook (lumenify_tps_supply_matrix_v1.xlsx) contains a toy model to convert your traffic into tokens/sec, map that to GPU throughput for two candidate model families, and compute a headroom buffer for SLA tiers.

What we need from Lumenify to lock this down:
- Peak and 95th-percentile concurrent requests per minute (by hour-of-day) over a typical weekday. If you don't have per-hour, an average daily profile + known peaks is ok.
- Typical average prompt+completion token lengths (or sample payloads).
- Preferred model family (MM-13B-q8 / MM-70B / opt-30b, etc.) and acceptable fallbacks for overload.
- Target P95 latency SLO for 95% of production traffic, and an absolute maximum latency for critical flows.

Assumptions in our workbook (highlighted): tokenization factor 1.05 (whitespace/punct), KV-cache hit rate 30% for multi-turn sessions, batching at 128ms latency budget, and a standard headroom multiplier of 1.6 for burst coverage. If you prefer different defaults we can adjust.

Next steps: if you can send the profile and confirm the model family by EOD Monday we'll produce a formal commit recommendation (GPU count, reserve vs burst pool, estimated monthly committed tokens) and a short runbook for scaling fallbacks.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Deal Architect, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.inference.com | +1 415-555-0132

Attachment: lumenify_tps_supply_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 2 sheets)

From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@lumenify.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@lumenify.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 11:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning: initial supply-match matrix and asks

Thanks, Michael. Attaching our traffic extract and a short note from product. Quick answers inline and attached: we've uploaded two files (hourly_agg_weekday.csv and prompt_samples.json) to the Drive link you included.

Summary:
- Peak 5-minute concurrency (observed last 30 days): 220 requests (around 10:40am PT).
- 95th percentile 1-minute concurrency: 135 requests.
- Average tokens per request (prompt+completion): 980 tokens (prompt ~450 / completion ~530).
- Multi-turn sessions: avg length 4 messages, expected KV-cache hit rate ~25%.
- Preferred model: MM-13B-q8 for baseline; willing to fallback to MM-7B-quant for heavy bursts.
- P95 latency target: 600ms for interactive flows; for backend batch scoring non-critical flows can be 1.5s.

Procurement note: procurement looped in — they will need a cost estimate and expected committed monthly token volumes to generate an initial PO.

Sara Jensen
Head of Product, Lumenify
sara.jensen@lumenify.com

Attachment: hourly_agg_weekday.csv (CSV), prompt_samples.json (JSON)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@lumenify.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning: initial supply-match matrix and asks

Great — the traffic extract is very helpful. I ran a quick convert in the attached workbook with your numbers and here are the high-level outputs (ballpark, prior to engineering validation):

Key derived figures (baseline MM-13B-q8, batching budget 128ms, KV-hit 25%):
- Average tokens per second (observed 95th window): 135 concurrent reqs * 980 tokens / avg response time window ~ 132,300 tokens/sec (before cache savings).
- Effective tokens/sec after KV-cache and tokenization factor: 132,300 * (1 - 0.25) / 1.05 ≈ 94,700 tokens/sec.
- Per-GPU sustained throughput estimate (MM-13B-q8, q8): ~9,000 tokens/sec with our runtime settings (128ms batch latency target).
- Required GPUs (sustained) = ceil(94,700 / 9,000) = 11 GPUs.
- Apply headroom multiplier 1.6 (burst + margin): recommended committed slab = 18 GPUs, with a 3-GPU shared burst pool for failover to cheaper fallback model (MM-7B) for excess load.

Notes and questions:
- The per-GPU throughput above is conservative; with sequence-length skewing and higher batching it can improve to ~11–12k tok/s, but we prefer conservative numbers for contractual commitments.
- Are there any hard limits on latency for the interactive flows beyond P95=600ms? We used 600ms as the limit when sizing using 128ms batching; if you need 400ms we will need more GPUs or to accept a lighter model.
- For the fallback path, we propose automatic routing to MM-7B-quant with a throttled burst pool; can you confirm any quality thresholds where fallback is unacceptable?

I'll ask Karthik to validate kernel-level numbers and map to A100 vs H100 options in the Dedicated pricing sheet.

—Michael

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning: initial supply-match matrix and asks

Adding engineering sizing detail — I validated the per-GPU throughput assumptions against our internal runbench for MM-13B-q8 under a 128ms latency target. A few concrete items:

- Measured sustained throughput (128ms budget, avg seq=980, batcher latency target 128ms): 9.2k tok/s on an A100-80GB using our optimized kernel set; H100 baseline improves to ~13.5k tok/s under same conditions.
- With KV-cache hit rate 25% effective tokens reduced ~25%, matching Michael's math.
- For redundancy and rolling maintenance we recommend 20% additional GPUs beyond the committed slab. So committed slab 18 (Michael) -> operational pool target = 22 GPUs.
- Burst strategy: 3 GPUs sized for MM-7B-quant (each ~28k tok/s) gives peak cushion ~84k tok/s for spikes; combined with routing to hosted fallback for non-sensitive traffic that should cover 99.9th percentile observed spikes.
- Cost tradeoff: H100s reduce committed count to ~12 GPUs but increase per-GPU unit cost — we'll provide both A100 and H100 TCO in the formal proposal.

I'm attaching a short cheat-sheet (inline table in the workbook) with per-GPU tok/s vs latency buckets to help procurement pick pricing/commit levels.

--Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

This looks good — thanks everyone. A few clarifications from procurement:

- Procurement wants the committed monthly token estimate (not just GPUs). Can you provide committed tokens/month aligned to the 18 GPU slab + 1.6 headroom?
- Can you provide a one-page note comparing the two options (A100 slab 18 + burst vs H100 slab 12 + burst) with committed token volumes and estimated monthly spend for each?
- We'll draft an initial PO once we have the committed token figure and an indicative monthly price. Our timeline: procurement would like to circulate a PO for internal review next Wednesday.

Confirmed: falls back to MM-7B-quant for spikes is acceptable for non-interactive flows; for interactive-critical flows product will accept up to 10% requests routed to fallback but any higher must be flagged.

I'll take your workbook and the PO stub (attached) back to procurement.

—Sara
Sara Jensen
Head of Product, Lumenify
